Why does Legion's onboarding lose patients?

Long image

A

Answer

The flow is built around insurance, payment and scheduling, not the patient. It first asks why someone is here on screen 10 of 17, and the funnel drops are symptoms of that order.

  1. 12 of the care flow's 17 screens serve business needs; 2 ask what the patient needs.
  2. When the patient does explain, the next screen sorts clinicians by earliest opening and ignores it, including a suicide disclosure.
  3. The measured portal keeps 23.8% of sessions to the payment page; two steps cause 67% of the loss.1
  4. Insured patients see "Perfect match found", then every matched clinician is fully booked.

Applies tov2 current-state analysisTexas patient personaJay's two OpenScreen walkthroughs, Nov 5, 2026PostHog portal sessions, 30 days to Aug 29, 2026

Safety stays early

Safety checks are a patient need too. A patient-first flow keeps them early and frames them as care, not as a gate. The portal asks about conditions first, but its match is still decided by plan and open slots.

Red steps are where Jay hit friction in the walkthroughs. Grey steps worked, or drew no complaint. The red dashed path is the returning-user jump from Round 1.

  1. Marketing site ↗

    Friction. Both buttons go straight to booking, and every top-rated specialist shows no availability. Jay: "Browse providers is not where I would start because I don't have much of an understanding." (O-01, O-02)

  2. Pick state ↗

    No friction. Texas or Utah, one tap.

  3. Email and code ↗

    Friction. The account comes before any question about care, and a returning email jumps straight to Find a provider. Jay: "Sign up before you even know what I'm looking for." (O-03, O-04)

  4. Plan or self-pay ↗

    Friction. Carrier logos only, with no member ID or coverage check. Jay: "What if the email is not connected to one of these accounts?" (O-05, O-06)

  5. Name, phone, address ↗

    Friction. The birth date defaults to 1996, and the address isn't validated. Jay: "I don't even know if this address is true or not." (O-07, O-08)

  6. Safety questions ↗

    Not marked. Jay called the 911 check "a good call". It asks about the account holder only, and Legion excludes minors. (O-09)

  7. Reasons, meds, free text ↗

    Friction and a safety gap. 14 diagnostic labels; "suicidal thoughts" typed here drew no follow-up. Jay: "I'm actually not sure yet because I don't know these terminologies." (O-10, O-11, O-12)

  8. Records consent ↗

    Not marked. Jay read it as "Build your health profile. Great." The missing opt-out is a design gap he didn't call out. (O-13)

  9. Find a provider ↗

    Friction. Sorted by earliest opening, with no reason to choose and no filters; changing insurance means a phone call. Jay: "So is availability really the promise that we want to show?" (O-14, O-15)

  10. Confirm and card ↗

    Friction. Jay stopped here. $250 with no breakdown or charge date, and manual card entry. Jay: "I don't know what I'm paying for, when I'm gonna be paid." (O-16, O-24)

Where does the portal flow cause friction?

Diagram structure
  • Portal sign-in login
  • Conditions cond
  • Insurance ins
  • Needs needs
  • Match page match
  • All fully booked booked
  • cond → ins
  • ins → needs
  • login → cond
  • match → booked · insured
  • needs → match

Red steps are where Jay hit friction. The fit check page, the portal's biggest drop, never appeared in either walkthrough, so it isn't drawn.

  1. Portal sign-in ↗

    No friction. Email link or Google sign-in.

  2. Conditions ↗

    Friction. The same account is asked again, with 7 options instead of 14. Jay: "I'm the same account, I don't know why you're asking me again." (O-17)

  3. Insurance ↗

    Friction. "We accept your plan, $0–$40 per session" with no member ID. Jay: "What is the scope? Is this based off of my plan?" (O-19)

  4. Needs ↗

    Not marked. Jay found the question useful but misplaced: "This question exists, but it exists at a different point." (O-18)

  5. Match page ↗

    Friction. "Perfect match found", then a banner that every clinician on the plan is unavailable. Jay: "Perfect match found, how? On what basis?" (O-20, O-21)

  6. All fully booked ↗

    Friction and a dead end for UnitedHealthcare, BCBS and Aetna. Jay: "If everybody's booked, why am I here? You have nothing to give me." (O-22, O-23)

This funnel covers the portal flow only

The marketing site's Book Appointment Now leads into the care flow, which has no funnel data in the brief. Payment-page reach is the last milestone. Payment success and the first visit are not tracked.
